seconds-please.sampleText: L READ THIS FIRST Your Table,Your Rules et’s get one thing straight before anyone passes the gravy: there’s no w rong w ay to do Thanksgiving. Maybe you’re squeezed around a table for twenty with the whole extended crew. Maybe it’s a few of you and a very small turkey. Maybe it’s just you this year. A ll of it counts. Some of you will host every single year. Some of you will never host, and you’re the hero who brings the ice. Some of you will potluck it, because one oven was never meant to carry a whole holiday. This year you could: Go all in: the full turkey dinner, a houseful of family and the whole party. Classic for a reason. Lace up and take a hike. Pack pie. Plan an adventure somewhere you’ve never been. Find a community table and pull up a chair. Head to your favorite restaurant or bar and find your people there. Invite friends over if you love to cook. Potluck it if you don’t. Throw out the menu. Tacos and tamales. Greek lamb and baklava. A full vegetarian spread. Nobody’s calling the turkey police. And yes, some of us skip the turkey completely, eat pumpkin pie for dinner and catch a new movie at the theater. Also valid. Extremely valid. Your Thanksgiving gets to change as your life changes. The season you’re in gets a vote. So does your heart. Use what works in these pages. Read them at a big table, a small one, a picnic table at the trailhead or a bar stool. Skip what doesn’t fit. The point is the thank-you, and thank-yous multiply. SECO NDS, PLEASE CHAOTICSUNSHINE.CO M · 2 no turkey police here

the-road-out-of-moab.sampleText: 1 · LESSON RECAP 2 · BACK STORY 3 · TALK IT THROUGH 4 · MEMORY CARDS 5 · COLORING PAGE LESSON RECAP Grandma survived it. Mom managed it. You get to end it. Ruth came from Moab, a family line with a painful start. When her husband died, she had every reason to go back to what she knew. Instead she told Naomi, "Your people will be my people and your God my God" (Ruth 1:16). One choice, made with help and walked out one ordinary day at a time, started a new line that led to King David and to Jesus. What ran in your family doesn't get to run your house just because it got here first. What got handed down What Ruth chose GOD Chemosh, the god of Moab (1 Kings 11:7) "Your God my God" (Ruth 1:16) PEOPLE Go back to her mother's house (1:8) Stay with Naomi (1:16-17) FUTURE Shut out "to the tenth generation" (Deuteronomy 23:3) Written into Jesus' family tree (Matthew 1:5) TAKE THIS HOME Peace lives here now. you can love where you came from and still take a different road. In Romans 8:12-17, Paul says the Spirit doesn't make you a slave to fear. It brings about your adoption and puts a family word in your mouth: "Abba, Father." In the Roman world, adoption was a legal act with teeth. In many cases old debts were canceled, the old name set aside, and the adoptee got full heir rights. In Christ, daughters get them too. before-the-first-mountain.sampleText: 1 · LESSON RECAP 2 · BACK STORY 3 · TALK IT THROUGH 4 · MEMORY CARDS 5 · COLORING PAGE LESSON RECAP By 7 a.m. you're keeping score. God settled it before time began. Most of us live as if God's choice gets renewed each morning based on the last 24 hours. Good day, He's pleased. Bad day, we brace. Paul places your chosenness before time itself: "For he chose us in him before the creation of the world" (Ephesians 1:4). You were chosen when you had done nothing at all, so your doing was never the reason. And Paul names the motive in two words: "In love." The scoreboard says Ephesians 1 says WHEN Renewed every morning, based on the last 24 hours "Before the creation of the world" (1:4) WHY Because you performed well enough "In love" (1:4-5) COST You keep paying, every day Grace "freely given" (1:6), sins forgiven (1:7) TAKE THIS HOME I was chosen before I did a thing. the scoreboard doesn't get a vote.
